name: Zul'Mashar
summary: In northeastern Eastern Plaguelands, the Mossflayers cling to Zul'Mashar and its ruins. Their ancient capital was broken by wars with human kingdoms, then ravaged by the Plague of Undeath.

sections.title: A Falling Stronghold
sections.body:
Before the Scourge crossed northern Lordaeron, Zul'Mashar was the seat of power for the Mossflayer forest trolls. Years of border skirmishes with Lordaeron's humans broke their lands into fragments. Then the Plague of Undeath swept through the region, striking trolls and humans alike.

Mazra'Alor's great stepped ziggurat still rises above the ruins, though little else remains of the capital's former glory. Warlord Thresh'jin and Zul'Brin Warpbranch command the surviving trolls, who cling to their ancient home. Many do not see the Scourge beginning to turn their own kin into rotting monstrosities.

sections.title: Infiltration from the Shadows
sections.body:
Within Zul'Mashar, a threat creeps through the Mossflayers' ranks. They guard their ziggurat and struggle to keep their independence in the ruined north, while hidden agents move among them and rot spreads. Infiltrator Hameya scouts among the ruins as living warriors gradually succumb to undeath.

No grand battle marks the end of this struggle. The once-proud stronghold edges toward falling under the Lich King's sway.

faq.answer: The Mossflayer forest trolls hold Zul'Mashar under Warlord Thresh'jin and Zul'Brin Warpbranch. Their grip weakens as the undead plague spreads through their society.
Mazra'Alor is the stepped troll ziggurat within Zul'Mashar. It is the architectural heart and spiritual center of the Mossflayer tribe's ancestral capital.
Long conflicts with Lordaeron's human kingdom wore Zul'Mashar down, and the Plague of Undeath ravaged it. The blight ruined the surrounding land, leaving the Mossflayers isolated and weakened.

faq.q: Are the trolls here allied with the Scourge?
faq.answer: No. The living Mossflayers fight outsiders to protect their ancestral lands. Meanwhile, the Scourge secretly infects and converts their people into undead.

angles.text: As a Darkspear troll, you can see the Mossflayers' plight at Zul'Mashar as a grim warning to isolated tribes that cling to ancient hatreds instead of finding allies in a changing world.
As Forsaken, you may watch Zul'Mashar with wary pragmatism, wondering whether the decaying Mossflayers will resist or swell the Scourge's ranks as zombified forest trolls.
